candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis, Section XXVII.27. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13, ed. J. Gwynn / Schaff (1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 360 AD)

'See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed'. Ephrem treats Isaac's olfactory blessing of Jacob as the prototype of every sacramental aroma: Israel-in-Jacob bears the fragrance of Eden (the field-which-the-Lord-blessed = the Edenic garden, by Ephrem's reading). Tewahedo liturgical use of frankincense in the qǝddase preserves this aroma-as-blessing pattern: the church fills with the smell of paradise.
